claim: XREF-CORE source checking must keep MW/PWG lexical shared-core rows separate from PWG/MW prefix-convention hub controls.

packetLabelVocabulary.label: lexical-shared-core
packetLabelVocabulary.meaning: The same source lemma points to the same meaningful Sanskrit target in MW and PWG.

packetLabelVocabulary.label: prefix-convention
packetLabelVocabulary.meaning: The target is primarily a prefix or compound-reference convention, not rare lexical inheritance.

packetLabelVocabulary.label: edition-continuity
packetLabelVocabulary.meaning: A stable edge across editions of the same dictionary family.

packetLabelVocabulary.label: lexical-target
packetLabelVocabulary.meaning: A top xref target that behaves like an ordinary lexical target rather than a convention hub.

packetLabelVocabulary.label: normalization-risk
packetLabelVocabulary.meaning: A target string where normalization may create or hide an edge.

packetLabelVocabulary.label: too-sparse
packetLabelVocabulary.meaning: A pair has too few shared sources for lineage interpretation.

selectionPolicy: Read the existing xref hub review artifact and xref edge CSV.
Keep the established 40-row MW/PWG shared-core sample in its current order.
Select the first five prefix-convention top targets for PWG and MW as controls.
Attach up to three dictionary source pointers per prefix target from xref_edges.csv order.
Record labels as source-check prompts, not accepted lineage decisions.
